messages:
Ellen (AE): New RFP: global payments company wants Private deploy. Must preserve original client 5-tuple (no SNAT), have stable egress IPs for allowlist, and a contractual burst credit (2x baseline sustained for 15m). Can we outline feasible topologies and any deal blockers?
Marco (SE): High-level: 1) TGW or VPC peering required to keep L4 src intact; Interface VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) cannot guarantee OS-level src IP — we can add X-Forwarded-For but that's app-layer. 2) Static egress needs reserved EIP pool or dedicated egress appliances.
Carlos (Customer): We operate hybrid: AWS + Azure. For AWS we can use TGW; for Azure they'd prefer ExpressRoute to a partner-managed cloud router. Will that work?
Nadia (NetOps): Short answer: yes, but must validate cross-cloud routing. For AWS: TGW attachment + explicit route to connector subnets keeps client IPs. For Azure: ExpressRoute + private peering to our managed VNet (or partner transit) can preserve src if no SNAT is performed in the path. In both cases avoid any in-path NAT or load-balancer that performs SNAT.
Pri (Solutions Eng): Firewall/allowlist checklist (shareable):
```
- Allow inbound to connector subnets (we will provide CIDRs) on TCP/443
- Allow healthcheck from connector health CIDR on TCP/80
- DNS: allow outbound to customer resolver; if not possible, allow to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 per policy
- Routes: add route table pointing to TGW/ExpressRoute for connector CIDRs
- MTU: test for 1500; account for extra overhead if IPsec
```
Also note: if you must terminate TLS at a corporate inspection appliance, that appliance must be placed before any SNAT and be approved by compliance.
Ellen (AE): Pricing & SLA asks: can we price reserved eip + burst credits and include a burst SLA?
Marco (SE): We can offer two commercial options: (A) Reserved Dedicated cluster (recommended) — pre-provisioned capacity for steady load; burst headroom achieved by pre-warmed standby nodes. This can carry a throughput SLA (SLO) if contracted. (B) Shared Private pool with burst credits — cheaper but bursts are best-effort. Ballpark: baseline cluster for 300 rps ~ $11k/mo; dedicated burst addon ~ 30% extra. Need Finance to finalize.
Nadia (NetOps): Operational caveats:
- EIP quotas: request reserved EIPs early; on-demand allocation may be rate-limited
- TGW propagation can take time; schedule routing changes in maintenance windows
- Disable source/dest check on any routed instances we deploy that act as routers
- Ensure Security Groups are explicit; don't rely on broad 0.0.0.0/0 rules for audit environments
InfraBot: Preflight checklist created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hybrid-private-preflight (contains TGW, ExpressRoute, EIP reservation steps, and test scripts).
Carlos (Customer): Do you have a short paragraph we can put in our vendor security questionnaire about client IP handling and connectivity options?
Pri (Solutions Eng): Draft paragraph for questionnaire: "Redwood Private supports Transit Gateway attachments, VPC peering, Interface VPC Endpoints, and partner-assisted ExpressRoute/Direct Connect. To preserve transport-layer client IPs, customers should use TGW or VPC peering (AWS) or direct/private peering (Azure) and avoid any SNAT in the path. If Interface Endpoints are chosen, Redwood can surface client identity at application layer via X-Forwarded-For headers. Static egress IPs are available via reserved EIP pools or dedicated egress instances; BYOIP arrangements supported in select regions."
Ellen (AE): Next steps: 1) Marco to sketch 1-page hybrid topology diagram (AWS TGW + Azure ExpressRoute) and a one-liner allowlist by EOD. 2) Nadia to kick off EIP quota request and confirm if any region quotas block burst. 3) Schedule technical deep-dive Wed 9am UTC with customer's infra + our infra.
Carlos (Customer): Wed 9am UTC works. One final ask: for our audit we need assurance that logs will include original client IPs if we choose peering. Can you confirm?
Nadia (NetOps): Confirmed: if traffic flows via TGW/peering with no SNAT, connector instances will see original src IPs and logs will include the 5-tuple. We'll document this in the arch diagram and add a validation step in the runbook (tcpdump/traceroute).
Ellen (AE): Thanks team 99I'll send the invite and attach the preflight runbook. :white_check_mark:
